turns.content: For diamond and graphite in equilibrium, write the Clapeyron relation for the slope of their coexistence curve in pressure-temperature space.
Calculate the phase-property differences needed in the Clapeyron relation from the supplied diamond and graphite data, converting the molar-volume difference to m^3/mol.
Evaluate the coexistence-curve slope in Pa/K and bar/K, stating the sign convention explicitly.
Use that local slope to estimate the signed pressure change for a 100.0-K temperature increase.
Report the pressure change in pascals and bar, and verify its direction from the chosen diamond/graphite phase-property differences.
What approximation is made by applying a constant local slope across the full 100.0-K interval?
Independently multiply the local slope by 100.0 K to check the finite pressure change numerically.
Qualify the estimate by explaining how temperature-dependent phase properties and curvature of the coexistence curve could affect it.
Give the final pressure change and direction, and summarize how the Clapeyron relation determines them.
